data.title: U.S. Stock Futures Flat as Traders Await Fed Rate Decision
data.description:
U.S. stock futures were steady on Monday evening as traders awaited the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision later this week. Futures on the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), the Nasdaq 100 (NDX), and the S&P 500 Index (SPX) were down 0.03%, 0.03%, and 0.05%, respectively, at 6:30 p.m. EDT on September 14.

Major U.S. stock indices closed lower on Monday as Treasury yields climbed and chip stocks led the drop. AI-linked stocks dragged the market lower after Anthropic's CEO called for slower frontier‑model development and OpenAI's Sam Altman ruled out an IPO this year. The Nasdaq, the S&P 500, and the Dow Jones fell 0.6%, 0.5%, and 0.3%, respectively.

In key economic reports tomorrow, the Empire State Manufacturing Survey will be released on Tuesday. The survey is a monthly report from the New York Fed that tracks how factories in the state are doing. It measures things like new orders, hiring, shipments, and overall business conditions to give a quick read on the health of the region's manufacturing sector.

data.title: Corning Stock (GLW) Plunged Over 13% on Monday – Here's What Spooked Investors
data.description:
Corning (GLW) shares dropped 13.6% on Monday after the company said it will sell up to $2 billion in new stock through an at‑the‑market program with Goldman Sachs (GS). The slide comes due to a mix of dilution worries and rising fear about AI spending. Following the deal, Mizuho Securities analyst John Roberts, CFA, maintained a Buy rating on GLW stock and cut the price target to $180 from $210.

GLW stock has climbed over 65% so far this year, aided by AI fiber deals and strong demand for optical parts. Thus, the surprise capital raise gave traders a reason to lock in gains.

Corning is a manufacturer of specialty glass, ceramics, and advanced optical products.

Promotion

Two ETFs for long or short leverage on COHR

Details About the Deal

Goldman Sachs is the sole sales agent on the deal. Corning said the net proceeds will go toward general corporate needs, using a shelf registration filed earlier this year. This setup has no set price and no set share count, giving Corning full control over when and how much stock it sells.

This setup is driving the sharp reaction as holders have no clear way to know when new supply might hit the market after a big run‑up in the stock this year.

Capex Gaps and Capital‑Heavy Optical Builds Raise Questions

Roberts noted Corning's long-term Springboard plan calls for strong free cash flow growth, but some parts of the optical business, like glass fiber furnaces, are capital heavy. The equity program looks like a simple backstop to make sure Corning can finish major projects even if customer capex or market conditions shift.

He also said Corning has not shared clear base case capex needs for its 2030 targets, including a 50% boost in glass fiber output. Capital intensity varies across solar wafers, downstream solar, optical cores, and cables, with cables and connectors being the least costly.

AI Spending Jitters Add Sector-Wide Pressure

The optical hardware sector depends on Big Tech's large AI data center budgets. Over the weekend, leaders from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Elon Musk publicly urged slowing frontier AI development.

Even though the leaders did not ask to cut capex, the comments sparked worries that cloud giants may cool hardware spending. That pressure is dragging down other optical names like Coherent (COHR), Fabrinet (FN), and Lumentum (LITE).

Is GLW a Good Stock to Buy Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on GLW stock based on seven Buys and three Holds assigned in the past three months. Further, the average Corning price target of $188.75 per share implies 31.44% upside potential.

data.title: Paramount Skydance (NASDAQ:PSKY) Stock Gains After Pulling Out of Netflix Agreement
data.description:
Entertainment giant Paramount Skydance (PSKY) has had an agreement running for some time now with Netflix (NFLX) over animated product released on Netflix's platform. A new report from Deadline, meanwhile, says that the pact is now over, and Paramount's animated content will have a new home. The news was welcome for investors, who sent Paramount shares up nearly 3% in the closing minutes of Friday's trading. Paramount has seen a 42.95% loss in its share price over the past year.

Out at Netflix, Sort Of

The deal, noted the report, comes from a previous arrangement between Netflix and Skydance Animation, back when Skydance Animation was a thing separate from Paramount. When Paramount became Paramount Skydance, Skydance Animation got folded into Paramount. Now, the agreement between Netflix and Skydance Animation is gone, because the agreement ran out, and there is no more Skydance Animation to have a deal with.

Paramount plans to continue licensing substantial amounts of content to Netflix. And it seems as though the Skydance Animation content will still come back to Netflix. A joint statement from the two companies noted, "Netflix and Paramount have mutually agreed to conclude their animated film agreement. Both companies remain fully committed to the successful releases of Ray Gunn and the untitled Jack and the Beanstalk project on Netflix, and additionally will continue their longstanding content licensing relationship. We are proud of our collaboration to date and look forward to bringing these upcoming films to audiences around the world."

data.title: Software Stocks CrowdStrike (CRWD) and Palo Alto Networks (PANW) Are Surging Today – Here's Why
data.description:
Software stocks, such as CrowdStrike (CRWD) and Palo Alto Networks (PANW), have surged about 15% and 14%, respectively, on Monday. This comes as investors rotate into cybersecurity software after top AI leaders warned about the risks of fast‑moving frontier AI systems.

Over the weekend, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged the industry to slow advanced AI development. This call was backed by OpenAI's Sam Altman, Elon Musk of SpaceX (SPCX), and Demis Hassabis of Google (GOOGL) DeepMind.

Their comments led to a broad market shift. Chip and hardware stocks fell on fears of an AI slowdown. Meanwhile, security software names surged as investors bet that protecting autonomous AI systems will remain a top priority.

Promotion

Two ETFs for long or short leverage on SPCX

Reasons Why CrowdStrike Stock Gained

Apart from investors moving into software names, CrowdStrike rallied after CEO George Kurtz said that even if AI development slows, autonomous cyber threats will keep rising, pushing firms toward modern, cloud‑native defense tools.

Further, CNBC's Jim Cramer called CrowdStrike a "must‑own" stock as machine‑speed attacks become more common.

Moreover, Wedbush analyst Steven Wahrhaftig started coverage on CRWD stock with a Buy rating and a $250 target, pointing to fast ARR growth and strong margins. He said CrowdStrike's Falcon platform is a core layer for AI‑native endpoint security, with cloud, identity, and SIEM tools giving the company a long growth runway.

Wahrhaftig added that M&A will stay key as CrowdStrike fills product gaps and wins more platform‑wide deals. Net new ARR is rising, and he sees 34% year-over-year growth in FY27 as more firms lean toward CrowdStrike to cut complexity and boost protection. He said the higher valuation is justified given the company's pace of profitable expansion.

Factors Aiding PANW's Surge Today

Palo Alto Networks is also climbing as investors treat cybersecurity as one of the most durable beneficiaries of the AI cycle. The stock is rebounding after a recent pullback, aided by strong fundamentals.

Also, Wedbush's Wahrhaftig initiated coverage of Palo Alto Networks at Buy with a $400 price target, adding the stock to its Best Ideas List. He said the company is the clearest winner in the push toward full‑platform security. Further, the analyst pointed to strong revenue growth, rising margins, and a steady M&A playbook that adds new modules without hurting cash flow.

Overall, Wahrhaftig believes PANW is well placed to capture the largest share of cyber budgets as firms move away from point tools and consolidate on one platform.

CRWD vs. PANW: Wall Street Sees More Growth Potential in Which Stock?

Wall Street currently sees more upside in PANW over CRWD. The TipRanks Stock Comparison Tool shows a Strong Buy consensus for PANW, with an average price target of $405.95, implying 8% upside. CRWD also has a Strong Buy consensus, with an average price target of $244.40, implying 3.3% upside from current levels.

data.title: Ford Stock (NYSE:F) Slips With News of 223,000 Recalled Vehicles
data.description:
Legacy automaker Ford (F) has been trying diligently to shake concerns about quality in its vehicles, and on many fronts, it succeeded. But it also finds itself in contention with a growing list of recalls. Today, another nearly 223,000 vehicles found themselves subject to recall, and over issues with the fuel tank. The news did not sit well with investors, and Ford shares dropped fractionally in Monday afternoon's trading. Ford has also seen a 19.61% rally in its share price over the past year.

A Pretty Important Recall, Too

The roughly 223,000 vehicles subject to recall here are being recalled over issues with the fuel tank, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). The tank may be "improperly secured," which in turn can cause the tank to "…leak fuel, or detach from the vehicle while driving." Such an issue can also "…cause an engine stall or increase the risk of fire."

Apparently, the fuel tank straps may have been improperly assembled, which could cause the leaks or outright detachment. Moreover, the only vehicles impacted by this are Ford F-150 models made between 2023 and 2027, which are some of Ford's biggest sellers. As ever, dealerships will take over on the front lines here, inspecting tank straps and replacing them where necessary.

A Push-to-Move Experience

Car and Driver, meanwhile, brought word of a new patent out of Ford that could have unexpected results. The patent describes a new way to move a truck very, very small distances by simply pushing it. For anyone who has ever hauled a load, and needed the load to be dropped in a very specific place, such a patent could represent a big help.

The patent is called "systems and methods for moving a vehicle using externally mounted HMI." Using the pop-up grab handle included on F-series trucks, the user would be able to effectively "nudge" the vehicle small distances with the grab handle. The movement right now seems limited to forward and reverse only, however. Such a system could be particularly useful in parking spaces; how often have you ever wished you could move just a little further into a space without restarting the car?

data.title: AI Will Be "Bigger than Oil, Gold, Diamonds, or even the Internet," Trump Says
data.description:

"AI, and Data Centers, will be the Greatest Economic Development Engine in History ­­— Bigger than Oil, Gold, Diamonds, or even the Internet," Trump said in a Truth Social post on Monday.

Trump Pushes Ahead on AI, Criticizes Permitting Delays
